words.sense: Actively kind and generous, seeking to help others
misconceptions: Assuming anything harmless counts as generosity.
Assuming a smile proves someone helped.

words.sense: Gentle or harmless, without harmful effect or intent
misconceptions: Assuming anything harmless counts as generosity.
Ignoring the difference between intent to help and absence of harm.

semantic_axes.description: Benevolent involves an active wish to benefit others; benign means gentle or harmless without requiring a helpful sacrifice.

edges.boundary_rule: Benevolent involves an active wish to benefit others; benign means gentle or harmless without requiring a helpful sacrifice.

misconceptions.M1: Assuming anything harmless counts as generosity.
misconceptions.M2: Assuming a smile proves someone helped.
misconceptions.M3: Ignoring the difference between intent to help and absence of harm.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Minho's comment to his cousin?

beats.text: Minho makes a light remark about their matching socks; his cousin laughs and remains completely at ease.
beats.decisive_clue: remark causes no hurt or threat
beats.reason: The initial evidence is remark causes no hurt or threat; it best supports benign.

beats.text: He makes the remark while holding a birthday cake.
beats.decisive_clue: remark causes no hurt or threat
beats.reason: The cake is incidental; the comment's lack of harmful effect matters.

chains.feedback_short: The cake is incidental; the comment's lack of harmful effect matters.
chains.feedback_deep: Benevolent means kindness expressed in helpful action; benign means not threatening or damaging. The cake is incidental; the comment's lack of harmful effect matters.
chains.contrast_rule: Benevolent does good; benign does no harm.

hints.axis: Benevolent involves an active wish to benefit others; benign means gentle or harmless without requiring a helpful sacrifice.
hints.contrast: Benevolent does good; benign does no harm.
